title: JSW Group Seeks Majority Stake in Volkswagen India as MoU Nears
excerpt: The Sajjan Jindal-led conglomerate is in advanced talks for a controlling interest in Skoda Auto Volkswagen India, with a preliminary agreement expected within two months.
body:
• JSW Group is in advanced talks to acquire a majority stake in Skoda Auto Volkswagen India, with a non-binding MoU expected within two months.
  • The deal would give JSW access to Volkswagen's European vehicle platforms and established production lines in India, while providing the German automaker with fresh capital.
  • Volkswagen has struggled to gain market share in India for over two decades, holding just 2.34% of passenger vehicle sales in FY26.
  • JSW is simultaneously building a 636-acre EV manufacturing plant in Maharashtra and expanding its battery cell production capacity to 30 GWh.

Sajjan Jindal's JSW Group is pushing for a majority stake in Volkswagen's India operations, according to people familiar with the matter, in a deal that could reshape the country's automotive landscape and bring a new Indian player alongside Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra.

The two sides are working toward a non-binding memorandum of understanding that could be signed within two months, with discussions centring on Skoda Auto Volkswagen India Pvt Ltd (SAVWIPL), the entity that runs Volkswagen, Skoda, Audi, Porsche, Lamborghini and Bentley brands in the country, Bloomberg News reported.

Three Years in the Making

JSW and Volkswagen first opened discussions three years ago, when the initial conversation focused on JSW potentially operating the German automaker's plants in Pune and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. The latest round of negotiations has expanded significantly — JSW is now seeking a controlling interest in the entire Indian subsidiary.

Top executives from both companies have met recently, though several critical issues remain unresolved, including the valuation of the business and the quantum of capital each side will invest. A Volkswagen spokesperson told Bloomberg the company "is constantly evaluating new business opportunities and various business options to implement its strategy in India." JSW did not respond to requests for comment.

"To fully explore the country's growth potential, we are always considering new business opportunities and are evaluating various options to ensure the best possible solution to implement our strategy in the highly dynamic Indian market."

— Skoda spokesperson

What Each Side Gains

For JSW, the deal would deliver instant access to Volkswagen's vehicle platforms, cutting years off the timeline needed to develop competitive automotive technology. The conglomerate already operates in the auto sector through its 35% stake in MG Motor India, acquired from China's SAIC in 2023, but those vehicles sell under the MG brand. A Volkswagen partnership would pave the way for JSW-branded vehicles built on proven European engineering.

For Volkswagen, the transaction would cap a years-long search for a local partner capable of injecting the capital needed to compete in the world's third-largest car market. Despite operating in India for more than two decades, the Volkswagen Group held just 2.34% of the passenger vehicle market in FY26, according to FADA data — behind Kia India's 5.94% and only marginally ahead of JSW's own MG Motor venture at 1.40%.

The German automaker has also scaled back its India EV ambitions, cutting planned investment in a new electric vehicle platform to about $700 million from an earlier commitment of $1 billion.

JSW's Automotive Ambitions

The Volkswagen stake is one piece of a broader automotive strategy. JSW is simultaneously developing a 636-acre EV manufacturing facility in Maharashtra with a total planned investment of Rs 27,200 crore, launching modular EV platforms under the JSW MG Motor joint venture, and building a 30 GWh lithium-ion battery cell manufacturing plant.

The conglomerate's steel business offers supply chain efficiencies for automotive manufacturing, while its investments in battery cells, EV components and charging infrastructure create what industry analysts describe as a full-stack EV ecosystem.

What's Next

Volkswagen's global leadership is expected to visit India in the coming weeks, a trip that could coincide with the signing of a preliminary agreement. However, the talks could still fall apart over valuation disagreements or capital commitment mismatches. Skoda Auto chief executive Klaus Zellmer has previously stated the brand would invest in India independently if the search for a local partner did not succeed — but with the Volkswagen Group under pressure to cut costs globally, finding a deep-pocketed Indian ally has become increasingly urgent.
